label: Production ID
description: System-assigned, set once on first save and never regenerated (Sprint 13 / 23.27).

elements.label: Project
elements.description: Links to the Project master. ID and name are copied down and snapshotted. Carried forward from the previous record on this device (Sprint 18) - a crew works one project all day.

elements.label: Contractor
elements.description: Links to the Contractor master. ID and name are copied down and snapshotted. Carried forward from the previous record on this device (Sprint 18).

elements.label: Work Date
elements.description: Deliberately NOT carried forward from the previous record: default_previous_value persists across days on a device, so the first entry of a new shift would silently inherit yesterday's date, and a mis-dated record corrupts the week, the forecast window and every per-day rate without tripping any check.

elements.label: Inspector
elements.description: The signed-in user at record creation, shown so a field user can see who raised this without running a query. The platform's own _created_by_id is the authority and is what reports join on.

elements.label: Crew
elements.description: Carried forward from the previous record on this device (Sprint 18).

elements.label: Route
elements.description: Carried forward from the previous record on this device (Sprint 18).

elements.label: Segment ID
elements.description: Derived from From/To structure, direction-normalized (Sprint 14).

elements.label: Work Category
elements.description: Carried forward from the previous record on this device (Sprint 18).

elements.label: Construction Method
elements.description: Carried forward from the previous record on this device (Sprint 18).

elements.label: Labor Code
elements.description: 146 pay units from the River City rate sheet.

elements.label: Quantity
elements.description: The quantity this production is billed on, in the unit shown below. For fiber placement measured in FT it fills in from the sequentials as soon as you enter them (Sprint 18) - record the range OR the quantity, not both. Anything typed here wins and is never overwritten.

elements.label: Unit
elements.description: Copied from the selected Contractor Rate, which is the authority on how a pay unit is measured. The Data Events runtime exposes no choice labels, so this can never be parsed out of the labor code (v7.4.0).

elements.label: From Structure
elements.description: Links the FROM structure in the structure master. Its ID and type are copied down, so the production record still resolves if the master changes. Leave blank and use the free-text From Location for a structure not yet in the master.

elements.label: To Structure
elements.description: Links the TO structure. Same copy-down as From Structure.

elements.label: Fiber Reel
elements.description: Links the physical reel. Its printed range is copied down so outside-range checks work offline.

elements.label: Reel ID
elements.description: Copied from the linked reel record.

elements.label: Sequential Footage
elements.description: ABS(End - Start). Direction-independent (Sprint 0.7).

elements.label: Total Installed Footage
elements.description: Sequential + Slack + Other. Components stay independently auditable (Sprint 0.9).

elements.label: Pull Count (derived)
elements.description: Read from the labor code. BM60(3)(1.25) = a 3-PULL bundled assembly.

elements.label: Conduit Diameter (derived)
elements.description: Read from the labor code, e.g. BM60(3)(1.25) = 1.25".

elements.label: Total Duct Footage (informational)
elements.description: Production footage x pull count = total DUCT feet in the ground. This is NOT the material quantity: a 3-pull package is one bundled assembly consumed at 1 FT per production FT. See Conduit Material Quantity below.

elements.label: Depth (inches)
elements.description: Contract minimum is 36-42 inches for most bore and trench units.

elements.label: Rock Encountered
elements.description: Rock adders BM60-R and BM71 are separately priced pay units - record them as their own production transaction.

elements.label: Trace Wire / Pull Rope Installed
elements.description: BM90 is a separate pay unit, billable only when no fiber is pulled at the same time.

elements.label: Conduit Material Code (derived)
elements.description: Canonical code CONDUIT-<size>-<n>PULL, derived from the labor code. 1.25" names the bundled n-PULL assembly; 2" and 4" always name the single-pipe 1PULL SKU and carry the pull count in the multiplier instead. The Labor-Material Mapping master resolves it to a stock part number.

elements.label: Conduit Material Quantity
elements.description: Production footage x the material multiplier. 1:1 for bundled 1.25 inch whatever the pull count; pull count x footage for single-pipe 2 inch and 4 inch (ruling 2026-09-17). Excludes the 10% purchasing waste factor, which lives in the mapping master.

elements.label: Span ID (derived)
elements.description: Direction-normalized from Pole ID and Previous Pole ID, so reversing them cannot create a second span.

elements.label: Span Footage
elements.description: Entered manually. Automatic derivation needs a pole/span dataset with coordinates, which does not exist yet - see docs.

elements.label: Anchors Installed
elements.description: AFO.GAA is a separate pay unit - record the production separately.

elements.label: Fiber Count at Location
elements.description: Total fibers in this closure. This determines WHICH HO-1 band prices the work.

elements.label: Priced Splice Band (derived)
elements.description: Read from the labor code, e.g. HO-1 (25-48) prices 25-48 fibers.

elements.label: Splice Quantity
elements.description: Fusion splices actually performed. This is the production quantity for HO-1 units.

elements.label: Measured Loss (dB)
elements.description: Typical fusion splice loss is under 0.10 dB.

elements.label: Applicable Contractor Rate
elements.description: Selecting a rate copies its price and provenance onto this transaction. The copy is PHYSICAL - later repricing of the master can never rewrite this record (Sprint 23.10 / 23.47.5).

elements.label: Contractor Rate
elements.description: Snapshot copied from the linked rate record. Read-only: a manual rate would break the audit trail.

elements.label: Rate Labor Code (snapshot)
elements.description: Compared against the selected Labor Code to catch a mismatched rate.

elements.label: Rate Project ID (snapshot)
elements.description: Blank means the rate applies to all projects.

elements.label: Extended Value
elements.description: Quantity x Unit Rate (Sprint 0.4).

label: MATERIALS

elements.label: Actual Material Used
elements.description: What the crew reports was actually consumed (Sprint 8).

description: What the crew reports was actually consumed. The EXPECTED quantity is not stored here: it is derived onto the record for conduit (Conduit Material Code and Quantity, under UNDERGROUND) and computed for every other family in reports/material-variance.sql. A device cannot read the mapping master, so a repeatable of calculated material could never have been filled in (Sprint 19).

elements.label: QA Status
elements.description: QA/QC outcome. An approval requires a recorded outcome that is not Fail and not Not Reviewed - an approval is a statement that somebody looked.

elements.label: QA Reviewer Outcome Detail
elements.description: What must be corrected, or the condition attached to a conditional pass. Required when the record is sent back - 'correction required' with no detail sends a crew back to site to guess.

elements.label: Correction Completed
elements.description: Set by the crew once the correction is done. Cleared automatically whenever the record is sent back again.

elements.label: Attachments
elements.description: Scans and documents supporting the review: permits, locate tickets, markups. Field photographs belong in Photos above.

elements.label: Exceptions (auto)
elements.description: Auto-populated by validation. Warnings do not block save (Sprint 18).

elements.label: Fingerprint - Strict (derived)
elements.description: Canonical signature of the same physical cable pull: project, contractor, date, pay unit, cable ID and the direction-normalized sequential range. Two records sharing this are near-certain duplicates - the same cable cannot be placed twice. Readable on purpose, so a reviewer can see which component differs.

elements.label: Fingerprint - Segment (derived)
elements.description: Canonical signature of the same work claimed twice between two structures, with no sequentials involved. Weaker evidence than the strict fingerprint, but it is the only duplicate signal available for boring, trenching and structure work.

elements.label: Fingerprint Strength (derived)
elements.description: How many identifying values this record actually carries. Below 4 the record cannot be reliably duplicate-checked, and reports ignore its fingerprints rather than reporting a false match.
